title: A magnet you can switch off

probes.question: What happens to an electromagnet's field when the current is turned off?
True or false: an iron core makes an electromagnet's field more powerful.

image.alt: A nail wrapped with coiled insulated wire and connected to a 9-volt battery, forming a simple electromagnet that holds small nails.

body.claim: An electromagnet is a magnet whose field is produced by an electric current, so the field disappears when the current is turned off.
body.why: Hans Christian Ørsted discovered in 1820 that electric currents create magnetic fields. Wrapping the wire into a coil around an iron core makes a more powerful magnet, and the strength of the field is proportional to the current through the winding.
